decisions.statement: One folder matches two shapes at once.
A shape reserves no term against a shape matching that same term.
No shape matches an empty folder.
A shape judges the files sitting in one folder.
Every subfolder is a folder of its own.
A subfolder named as an enabled shape's own name is a part rather than a stray.
Those names are the ones the enabled shapes publish.
Such a subfolder is judged of its own by the shape whose name that subfolder takes.
Passing such a subfolder over as a part loses no judgement.
A shape whose subject is a folder of one name reads no folder of another name.
The files a part holds are judged where that part is judged.
A shape reads the folders sitting directly under the folder that shape judges.
A shape reads the files sitting directly in any folder the shape names.
A shape reads the page type sitting alone in any folder the shape names.
A folder with no page type answers with nothing.
A folder with more than one page type answers with nothing too.
A page type answers with its slug.
A page type answers with every property slug that page type declares.
A page type declares the properties written on its own page.
A page type declares the properties every type above that page type declares.
A page type declares the fields of every record property in that page type's `properties` folder.
A page type declares the members every `one-of-property` in its `properties` folder names.
A folder with one page answers with the name that page gives its folder.
A page gives its folder its slug.
That name has the opening that name shares with the page above the folder taken off.
The opening is taken off again while the name left still opens with a name the page above has.
The name a folder answers with opens with no name the page above that folder has.
A folder answers with no name where taking that opening off leaves nothing.
That answer is a folder wanting a name rather than a folder wanting no name.
The folder with nothing above it answers with no name.
A folder with no page answers with nothing.
A folder with a page type beside a second page answers for the page type.
That second page is a domain of the page type's slug.
A folder holding more than one page otherwise answers with nothing.
A folder answers with the page type and the slug of each page in that folder.
A folder answers with the parts the page in that folder declares.
A folder answers with the parts the second page in that folder declares too.
A page answers with the files that page's own file properties land on.
The files a page answers with are read off the page rather than worked out from its name.
A page answers with the build folders that page's own folder properties name.
A page answers with the collections that page names as holding that page.
A page type gathers its pages under the plural that page type states.
A folder answers with every page type gathering its pages under that name.
A folder answers whether a page above that folder claims that folder.
A folder under a claimed folder answers that it is claimed too.
A file held beside a page under a reserved tail is a part of that page too.
A file whose ending a page's property names is a part of that page too.
A shape states its test.
A shape states whether the shape judges folders.
A shape judging no folder keeps its page.
A page is declared a part by its page type and slug together.
A folder holding a workspace beside a domain answers for the domain.

definition: a shape a folder is allowed to have
